chunks: From him, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a group of people who drown or are buried by a house collapsing; he said, 'They inherit from one another.'
ai.seo_question: How is inheritance distributed when multiple family members die in the same accident?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the ruling for simultaneous death (*al-mutawaffayan bi-mawtatin*) by stating they inherit from one another, a principle that prevents the estate from remaining in a state of uncertainty (*istibrah*). This ruling is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for resolving complex inheritance scenarios where the chronological order of death cannot be determined, ensuring the distribution of wealth proceeds without delay. It reflects the practical application of Quranic inheritance laws to real-world contingencies, emphasizing clarity and justice in familial wealth transfer.
